author: Show-Me State Times
title: Former St. Louis circus official pleads guilty to embezzlement
text:
Thomas C. Albus, United States Attorney | Official Website
Thomas C. Albus, United States Attorney | Official Website
A former board member and president of a St. Louis-based non-profit circus pleaded guilty in federal court to embezzling more than $123,000 from the organization over a period spanning December 2022 through at least September 2023.
George S. Pace, 63, of Ladue, admitted to four counts of wire fraud during proceedings in U.S. District Court in St. Louis. According to the plea agreement, Pace used credit cards obtained without the circus’s knowledge or approval to pay for personal expenses such as nail salons, restaurants, skin care treatments, and horseback riding activities. When another official discovered questionable charges on one of the cards, Pace falsely claimed it had been stolen and presented forged account statements indicating he had resolved the charges.
Pace also redirected checks from the circus’s bank account for his own use instead of paying down a line of credit as intended. This diversion led to additional interest costs for the organization. Additionally, he deposited donor checks made out to the circus into his personal account. In total, Pace acknowledged defrauding the non-profit out of $123,015.94.
Pace further admitted in his plea agreement that he fraudulently applied for two U.S. Small Business Administration Disaster Assistance Loans totaling $29,400; both applications were denied by the SBA.
Sentencing is set for May 4. Each count of wire fraud carries a possible sentence of up to 20 years in prison and a fine up to $250,000.
The FBI conducted the investigation into this case. Assistant U.S. Attorney Gwendolyn Carroll is handling prosecution.
